content_type_gate.charset: a charset parameter must satisfy parser_policy.text_decoding_v1.http_charset_policy (UTF-8 compatible); otherwise PARSER_FAILED
content_type_gate.comparison: type/subtype compared ASCII case-insensitively; parameter names ASCII case-insensitive; parameter order irrelevant; after the duplicate check, parameters other than charset do not affect admission
content_type_gate.duplicate_parameter_name: any parameter name appearing twice within one value (case-insensitively) -> PARSER_FAILED
content_type_gate.field_name: Content-Type header field name matched ASCII case-insensitively
content_type_gate.header_absence_note: text_decoding_v1's recorded-header-absence input remains provenance only; an admitted body can never reach text decoding without passing this gate
content_type_gate.missing: no Content-Type field -> PARSER_FAILED; no sniffing
content_type_gate.multiple_values: each Content-Type field line is one value; if every value parses, all share the same case-folded type/subtype and each passes parser_policy.text_decoding_v1.http_charset_policy, the gate passes; otherwise PARSER_FAILED
content_type_gate.quoted_string: quoted-pairs are unescaped per RFC 9110 before the charset label is evaluated
content_type_gate.stage: after durable raw persistence (raw retained), before charset/text decoding
content_type_gate.unparseable_value: PARSER_FAILED (including an unquoted comma, empty value or missing subtype)
content_type_gate.value_grammar: OWS type '/' subtype *( OWS ';' OWS [ parameter ] ) OWS (RFC 9110): empty parameters and a trailing ';' are allowed; type, subtype and parameter names are tokens; a parameter value is a token or quoted-string

decoded_body_limit_enforcement.accepted_buffer_rule: Start decoded_count at 0. For each incrementally produced decoded chunk, before appending, if decoded_count + len(chunk) > the applicable body limit, ABORT immediately without appending excess bytes. Otherwise append and increment decoded_count. The accepted decoded-body accumulation MUST never exceed the applicable cap.
decoded_body_limit_enforcement.basis: UNCHANGED raw_policy.bytes_semantics: HTTP entity-body bytes after all applicable transport/content decoding required by the frozen body-byte semantics, before any charset/text decoding. This rule changes WHEN the existing decoded-body limit is enforced, not the hashed/persisted/replay byte stage.

content_length_role.missing_or_misleading_value: The same decoded-body cap and incremental enforcement remain mandatory, including when Content-Length is absent, incorrect or smaller than decoded output.
content_length_role.permitted_role: Transport provenance or an early rejection hint only as already permitted by existing semantics; never a substitute for decoded-byte counting. Compressed-byte length and socket-byte length are not the decoded-size authority either.

decoded_body_limit_enforcement.decoded_output_production: Decoder output production itself MUST be incrementally bounded while enforcing the applicable decoded-body cap. Checking chunks after an unbounded decoding call has already materialized the complete expansion is NOT conforming. Stop decoding immediately when further output would exceed the cap; do not continue consuming/decompressing the remainder merely to determine final size.
decoded_body_limit_enforcement.encoding_scope: The same cap applies to identity, gzip, brotli or any other encoding ONLY insofar as it is already admitted by frozen V1 semantics. FIX8 adds no encoding support. A small compressed representation cannot bypass the decoded-body limit.

limit_boundary.pass_scope: Size gate only; successful complete-body admission still requires every other existing V1 check.

decoded_body_limit_enforcement.memory_guarantee_scope: The accepted decoded-body accumulation is bounded by the configured cap and decoded output production must stop at attempted excess. No total process-memory, constant-memory, exact RSS or decompressor-internal-memory guarantee is claimed. Library, chunk size, buffer layout and bounded decoding API are implementation choices; unbounded decompress-all followed by a size check is not.

oversized_body.partial_body_replay: FORBIDDEN - no incomplete prefix may be treated as a complete response, hashed as a normal successful complete body, or replayed/parsed as one. This fix introduces no partial-body replay or diagnostic hash semantics.
oversized_body.provenance: Retain transport/provenance and failure metadata only as already permitted by the existing design. An oversized decoded response MUST NOT be persisted or admitted as a valid complete raw body artifact.
oversized_body.source_health_binding: Reuse source_health.mappings['decoded body exceeds the frozen size bound']; no new global health state. Oversize is terminal for this response's normal capture pipeline.

decoded_body_limit_enforcement.pipeline_gate: An oversized response MUST NOT reach charset/text decoding, an XML parser, an HTML parser or the normalizer. No truncation-and-continue, parse-first-N-MiB or best effort.
decoded_body_limit_enforcement.raw_replay_preservation: For complete admitted bodies, existing hash bytes, persisted body bytes and offline replay input bytes remain unchanged. Raw-first persistence before parsing remains mandatory; no successful complete-body SHA-256 is manufactured from an aborted prefix.
decoded_body_limit_enforcement.redirect_scope: Applies where an HTTP body is consumed under existing V1 policy. Redirect identity, validation and follow rules are unchanged; this fix introduces no redirect-body parsing semantics.

http_status_policy.body_appearance_cannot_override_status: a 404 body containing perfectly valid-looking FOMC HTML is SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE with no HTML semantic parse, no event and no zero. A 500 body containing well-formed valid-looking Fed RSS is SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE with no feed success and no EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO.

covers_non_exhaustively: 3xx not successfully followed as an intermediate redirect

final_body_admission.rule: a final HTTP response body is eligible for NORMAL FOMC V1 content processing IF AND ONLY IF final_status_code == 200, by EXACT equality. NOT any 2xx, NOT status < 400, NOT "a body is present", NOT "the body looks valid".

http_status_policy.fix12_non_scope: FIX12 does NOT decide whether a 429, 500, 503 or timeout is retried - it only freezes that if such a response is the FINAL response of the logical attempt, it is non-admitted and maps to SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. Existing polling.retry_policy remains authoritative and unchanged. FIX14 binds redirect and permitted later reattempt accounting to request_accounting; FIX15 rate_limiter defines their shared temporal admission, without changing retry permissions or response admission.
gate_order: 2. record allowed transport/provenance metadata under existing semantics
3. classify the response as an intermediate allowed redirect, a final exact 200, or a non-admitted final/error response
4. ONLY a final exact 200 may enter normal complete-body acquisition, decoded-size enforcement, durable-body persistence, content hashing, text decoding and semantic parsing

no_content.rule: no accepted empty body, no successful content hash representing a valid statement or feed, no EventRevision, no EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO

http_status_policy.non_admitted_body_rule: a final non-200 body MUST NOT be used as parser input, and MUST NOT be hashed or persisted AS IF it were a successful admitted content body. Diagnostic transport provenance retained under existing raw primitives remains explicitly NON_ADMITTED.

not_modified.even_with_verified_prior_body: conditional caching and reuse remain unsupported even when a verified prior body exists. That prior body remains historical local data and is NOT substituted into this HTTP observation.
not_modified.rule: V1 does NOT reuse an old body in response to 304: no body hash, no new EventRevision, no reuse of a previous body, no synthesized body and no clean zero.
not_modified.why: deliberately avoids introducing a second cache/replay semantics into V1

partial_content.extends_fix8: this extends FIX8's "no incomplete prefix may be treated as a complete response" property to SERVER-DECLARED Partial Content. FIX8 covered truncation the CLIENT causes by aborting; 206 is incompleteness the SERVER declares, and arrives complete at the transport layer.
partial_content.rule: Range retrieval is unsupported in V1 and the client MUST NOT send Range or If-Range. A 206 received unexpectedly yields no successful body hash, no semantic parser input, no EventRevision and is never interpreted as a complete response.

http_status_policy.status_200_is_not_semantic_success: the status gate alone does NOT mean semantic success. An admitted body must still pass every existing gate: decoded-size bound, complete-body semantics, durable raw and hash, UTF-8, XML/HTML security, parser and classifier, and commit. 200 bypasses no existing validation.

http_policy.max_redirects_note: tightens urllib's default of 10; must be enforced explicitly

physical_attempt_deadline.address_policy: Resolved addresses are tried SEQUENTIALLY in resolver order, one TCP connection attempt at a time, each bounded by connect_timeout_seconds, all inside the same 60 s total deadline; the first established connection is used. No parallel or racing connection attempts (no Happy Eyeballs). All address attempts belong to ONE physical attempt and one unit. Resolution is one lookup with unspecified address family (IPv4 and IPv6), used in the order returned by the platform resolver.
physical_attempt_deadline.begins_at: PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START - the FIX15 grant-and-consume instant immediately before transport invocation
physical_attempt_deadline.boundary: An attempt succeeds at the network level only if its terminal network event occurs at monotonic elapsed e < 60 s from begins_at. At e = 60 s every unfinished attempt is expired.
physical_attempt_deadline.clock: MONOTONIC - the rate_limiter.clock domain of the current limiter epoch; wall-clock changes cannot shorten or extend it
covers: TCP connection establishment, including every resolved-address attempt
TLS handshake including certificate and hostname verification
content decoding required to produce admitted decoded body bytes
physical_attempt_deadline.ends_at: The network phase of an attempt ends when (a) the complete decoded body of a final exact-200 response is available, (b) the response is classified as an intermediate redirect or non-admitted final response, whose body is not drained (the connection is closed), or (c) the attempt fails.
physical_attempt_deadline.enforcement: At the total deadline the FOMC provider operation aborts the attempt logically. Observable requirements: a DNS result arriving after expiry is discarded; no TCP connection is initiated from it; no HTTP request byte is sent by the expired attempt; nothing received by it is admitted. Resolver activity inside the platform after logical cancellation (for example retransmissions of an abandoned lookup) is outside provider semantics unless the implementation chooses process isolation.

expiry.reobservation: obligation stays PENDING; further attempts follow revision_policy.reobservation_scheduler.retry_policy
expiry.zero: blocked for the affected feed cycle or candidate

physical_attempt_deadline.post_network_stages: Durable persistence, hashing, text decoding, parsing, classification, normalization and commit are local stages outside this deadline and perform no network I/O.

redirects.logical_fetch_deadline: No additional logical-fetch deadline. Every attempt is individually bounded and at most 4 exist, so no active network attempt runs forever; limiter waits are finite while FIX15 grants.
redirects.rule: Each redirect-follow request is its own PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START with its own fresh 60-second deadline beginning at its own grant. Limiter waiting between attempts is counted against no attempt.

physical_attempt_deadline.slow_drip: A server sending one decoded byte every 29 s never trips the 30 s inactivity bound, but the attempt is aborted at elapsed 60 s. No complete body is admitted.

stage_limits.classification_invariance: Whichever limit fires, the outcome class is the same: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, no admission.
stage_limits.connect_timeout_seconds: http_policy.connect_timeout_seconds = 10, unchanged: bounds each TCP connection establishment attempt
stage_limits.dns: No separate DNS limit; DNS is bounded by the total deadline.
stage_limits.earliest_limit_wins: Every applicable limit is enforced; whichever expires first ends the attempt. Stage limits never extend the total deadline.
stage_limits.read_timeout_seconds: http_policy.read_timeout_seconds = 30, unchanged: an INACTIVITY bound on each individual blocking socket read or write, including TLS handshake I/O, status/header wait and each body read

raw_first_and_status.admitted_final_200: the durable raw body exists before any normalized semantic visibility - the existing raw-first guarantee is unchanged
raw_first_and_status.clarification: raw-first does NOT mean "parse every HTTP body regardless of status"
raw_first_and_status.diagnostic_digest_note: if a separate low-level diagnostic transport digest already exists by design, it must not be confused with the admitted content hash
raw_first_and_status.non_admitted_status: transport and status provenance may be durable under existing primitives, but there is NO admitted complete content body eligible for normal semantic replay or parsing

http_policy.read_timeout_note: matches the repo convention REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 30; an inactivity bound whose coverage is frozen in http_policy.physical_attempt_deadline.stage_limits

redirect_implementation.automatic_redirect_following: FORBIDDEN - the HTTP client must never follow a redirect itself
redirect_implementation.connections: every physical attempt opens a new connection (its own DNS, TCP and TLS stages under its own deadline); no connection is reused across physical attempts
per_response: 1. read the status and headers of the response of the current physical attempt
2. if the status is an allowed redirect status: resolve Location under http_policy.redirect_policy (no URI-header fallback, no repair), validate the target completely BEFORE any network side effect
3. close the redirect response and its connection without draining its body; the redirect body is never semantic, never admitted and never read
4. obtain a separate FIX15 limiter grant for the next physical attempt, consuming one unit, with a fresh http_policy.physical_attempt_deadline
5. at most 3 followed redirects per logical fetch (http_policy.max_redirects); a 4th redirect is a redirect-limit failure
6. any other final status goes to http_policy.http_status_policy
redirect_implementation.timeouts: the transport must enforce connect_timeout_seconds and read_timeout_seconds separately, plus the total deadline

redirect_policy.allowed_statuses_rule: ONLY these intermediate redirect statuses may be FOLLOWED. A 3xx outside this set is a final non-admitted response: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.
redirect_policy.body_rule: bodies attached to intermediate 301/302/303/307/308 responses are never semantic feed or statement bodies: no XML/HTML semantic parse and no EventRevision from a redirect body. Retained transport diagnostics remain non-admitted and must never influence the classifier.
redirect_policy.fourth_redirect_rule: the fourth redirect Location target MUST NOT be requested; the logical fetch terminates with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE
redirect_policy.identity_rule: a final 200 reached through valid redirects may enter the normal pipeline, but identity remains the FIX4 authority: the official discovery link BEFORE redirects. The final URL stays non-identifying provenance and redirects NEVER re-key source_item_id.

algorithm.dot_segments: removed by the frozen reference-resolution algorithm. NO filesystem interpretation and NO local path normalization; the result is an HTTP URL passed to V1 security validation.

base.chain_rule: U0 requested -> Location L1 resolved against U0 -> request U1; U1 returns L2 resolved against U1 -> request U2. Later Locations are NEVER resolved against U0.
base.rule: the exact absolute request URL actually used for the CURRENT HTTP hop

fragment.must_not_hide_a_forbidden_component: removing the fragment must never conceal an otherwise forbidden query, host or scheme - every other URL check still applies to the resolved candidate
fragment.rule: resolution may produce a URI carrying a fragment; the already-frozen canonicalization then removes it from the actual HTTP request target. No second fragment policy is invented for redirects.

location_resolution.identity_rule: resolution derives only the next request_url for that transport hop. It NEVER changes canonical_primary_statement_url, source_item_id or the logical identity authority, which remains the official discovery link BEFORE redirects (FIX4) even across U0 -> U1 -> U2 relative chains.

location_value_preprocessing.trim_rule: remove ONLY surrounding HTTP optional whitespace (SP U+0020 and HTAB U+0009) from the beginning and end of the field value

order: 1. READ_LOCATION
2. TRIM_OUTER_HTTP_OWS (SP and HTAB only)
3. REJECT_EMPTY
4. PARSE_URI_REFERENCE
5. RESOLVE_AGAINST_CURRENT_REQUEST_URL
6. APPLY_EXISTING_V1_URL_SECURITY_AND_CANONICALIZATION
7. APPLY_EXISTING_FRAGMENT_NON_REQUEST_RULE
8. REQUEST_ONLY_IF_ADMITTED
location_resolution.order_rule: security validation MUST NOT be applied to the UNRESOLVED relative text as if it were already an absolute URL. Resolution precedes validation; validation is never weakened by it.

percent_escapes.rule: reference resolution MUST NOT percent-decode before FIX7 validation, and must apply no normalization that changes logical path semantics. Malformed forms such as %, %2 or %GG fail before any request.

location_resolution.redirect_body: UNCHANGED from FIX12 - non-semantic. Location derivation uses response METADATA only; a redirect body can never influence the target URL, the classifier, statement content or identity.
location_resolution.retries_untouched: FIX13 adds no retry rule; the existing frozen retry policy is unchanged.

security_after_resolution.no_special_redirect_security_regime: a resolved redirect target satisfies EXACTLY the same V1 constraints as any other URL. Being a redirect target grants no trust, and being absolute grants no special case.

supported_reference_forms.query_only_reference: syntactically resolvable, then subject to the unchanged V1 query policy

forbidden_heuristics: treating arbitrary text as a path
syntax.must_parse_as: exactly one URI-reference under the frozen resolution semantics

transition_accounting.rule: each successfully followed Location resolution consumes exactly ONE redirect transition from FIX12's maximum of 3. A REJECTED Location causes no target request and no transition follow; the response carrying it may still be recorded as transport provenance under existing semantics.

redirect_policy.location_rule: an allowed redirect status MUST carry a Location header. Its value is preprocessed, parsed as a URI-reference and RESOLVED against the current hop request URL per redirect_policy.location_resolution, and only the resolved absolute candidate is validated under the existing URL security and canonicalization rules. Missing Location, empty Location, a malformed reference or an unsafe resolved target all yield SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. The target is NEVER guessed or reconstructed.
redirect_policy.loop_rule: a loop such as A -> B -> A terminates via the redirect-transition limit at the latest. No hidden automatic redirect following beyond max_followed_transitions. An implementation may detect a loop sooner only if that alters no admitted content semantics; the frozen deterministic behaviour is the transition count.
redirect_policy.method_rule: FOMC V1 requests are GET only and every followed redirect remains a GET. No POST, no body-bearing redirect semantics, no library-dependent method choice.
redirect_policy.request_accounting: request_accounting applies independently before EVERY physical hop: a target admitted by FIX13 still must reacquire the shared provider limiter before any network side effect. HTTP auto-follow cannot bypass that gate.
redirect_policy.target_validation: before EACH redirect follow the target must pass all V1 redirect URL security checks - HTTPS, host allowlist, userinfo, port, percent syntax and the rest - and validation occurs BEFORE the network request, so an unsafe target is never contacted
redirect_policy.transition_semantics: max_redirects = 3 means AT MOST THREE FOLLOWED REDIRECT TRANSITIONS after the initial request. Initial request -> redirect #1 -> follow -> redirect #2 -> follow -> redirect #3 -> follow. If the response after following redirect #3 is itself another redirect, that is redirect #4.

http_policy.redirect_rule: validated BEFORE being followed; destination must stay on the allowlist; off-allowlist => fail closed, host never contacted
http_policy.user_agent_note: repo convention hyprl-trading-lab-<purpose>/<version>. No personal e-mail, no secret, no browser impersonation.

identity.aliasing_non_goal_v1: NO automatic alias equivalence or global deduplication across distinct normalized official discovery URLs is claimed. Different normalized identity URLs remain distinct logical source items unless an already-frozen conflict rule independently blocks admission. Do not merge using body hash, date, title, HTML canonical or final redirect destination; alias equivalence requires a separately frozen policy.
identity.canonical_primary_statement_url: normalize(official_discovery_link_before_redirect), where normalize is EXACTLY the existing url_canonicalization policy. The word canonical means the normalized official discovery-link URL selected by this identity policy; it does not mean the final response URL or a remote HTML canonical URL.
identity.canonical_url_boundary: FIX4 freezes WHICH INPUT enters existing URL normalization: the official discovery link BEFORE primary network redirects. URL normalization transforms and redirect security rules are unchanged. General alias resolution is not introduced. FIX3 date-correction stability remains intact.

conflict_policy.resolution: never 'latest wins'; persist conflict diagnostics and raw provenance; no trusted normalized event until a deterministic resolution policy admits it

date_correction.downstream_dedupe: D1 and corrected D2 are revision metadata of the SAME source_item_id; downstream MUST NOT count them as two independent logical FOMC events merely because the date changed
date_correction.existing_guid_conflicts: preserved unchanged; apply conflict_policy if independently triggered. A date correction by itself is NOT an identity conflict, and is never a reason to split the item.
date_correction.revision_metadata: official_statement_date belongs to the observed content revision. If H1/D1 becomes H2/D2 with a changed body hash, append a NEW immutable content revision under the SAME source_item_id. Retain H1/D1 intact; no overwrite. Identical-body discrepancies follow parser_policy.official_statement_date_determinism.
date_correction.rule: same provider_id + same event_family + same canonical_primary_statement_url => SAME logical source item, regardless of an official_statement_date correction
date_correction.visibility: each revision keeps source_available_at = null and source_updated_at = null, and its own actual observed_at and commit-bound ingested_at. Identity repair never rewrites observed_at, ingested_at or declared_release_at on an existing revision. D2 is metadata, not source_updated_at, correction timing or content-vintage evidence; no retroactive availability change.
date_correction.with_guid: same canonical primary URL and same RSS GUID with D1 -> D2: SAME source_item_id; append a revision if the body hash changes
date_correction.without_guid: same canonical primary URL in historical archive/backfill with no RSS GUID and D1 -> D2: SAME source_item_id; append a revision if the body hash changes. GUID absence does not alter logical identity.

identity.discovery_link_mutation: a change in the official discovery link from U1 to a differently normalized U2 is NOT a redirect-topology change. The existing item keeps its stored U1-derived identity. A newly discovered U2 follows existing conflict/dedupe semantics only; no alias inference, identity rewrite or 'latest URL wins'.
identity.final_response_url_role: NON-IDENTIFYING TRANSPORT PROVENANCE: final allowlisted response URL after redirects. It MUST NOT replace canonical_primary_statement_url or re-key an item, including when it differs from discovery or changes on a later observation. Existing security validation still applies.
identity.guid_note: historical statements may lie outside current feed depth; identity must not depend on the feed
identity.historical_discovery_url_role: the validated HISTORICAL_BACKFILL_MANIFEST_V1 entry (surfaces.backfill_manifest), persisted durably before any request, supplies the pre-redirect identity input under the same validation and normalization as LIVE. No synthesized URL from date; no RSS GUID required; no identity from final response or HTML canonical.
identity.html_canonical_role: NON-IDENTIFYING, NON-AUTHORITATIVE: <link rel="canonical"> is ignored for V1 semantics and logical identity. It MUST NOT replace canonical_primary_statement_url, change source_item_id, merge or split items, or override official discovery identity. A mismatch alone is NOT an identity conflict. If retained at all, it is optional diagnostic/provenance only; no network retrieval is authorized by this field.
identity.identity_url_input_stage: official statement link parsed from the already DURABLE official discovery artifact, BEFORE the primary HTTP request and BEFORE following any primary redirect
identity_url_order: 1. fetch and durably persist the official discovery artifact under existing raw-first/provenance rules
2. parse its official statement link U_discovered
3. validate U_discovered using existing V1 URL/security rules
4. apply the EXISTING frozen url_canonicalization policy to U_discovered
5. bind the resulting value as canonical_primary_statement_url
6. compute source_item_id from provider_id, event_family and that value using existing canonical_serialization
7. perform the primary HTTP request for the discovered statement under existing HTTP policy
9. persist the redirect chain and U_final as transport provenance under existing raw policy
identity.identity_url_precomputation: computing a candidate identity before the primary fetch does NOT admit an EventRevision or an IN_SCOPE_V1 event; existing primary classification, raw-first, normalization and commit-bound visibility requirements remain mandatory
identity.live_discovery_url_role: the official monetary-policy RSS item's <link> extracted from its durable feed artifact supplies the pre-redirect identity input. Validate it, apply existing normalization and derive source_item_id before primary redirects. RSS GUID remains discovery provenance/consistency signal only.
identity.missing_canonical_url: FAIL CLOSED under the existing identity policy if a stable canonical primary URL cannot be established. No date fallback, no (provider_id, event_family, date) fallback and no GUID+date fallback may manufacture a logical identity.

provenance_url_roles.discovered_url: official statement link extracted from the durable discovery artifact; only its existing-policy normalized value supplies the logical URL identity
provenance_url_roles.final_response_url: final allowlisted URL after primary redirects, corresponding to existing raw policy's final URL provenance
provenance_url_roles.redirect_chain: ordered transport provenance of the primary request hops
provenance_url_roles.request_url: URL actually requested at a given hop; transport provenance, not a replacement identity input after derivation
provenance_url_roles.storage_note: semantic roles within existing raw/observation provenance, not a new raw or normalized schema; keep discovery provenance distinct from request, redirect and final response provenance

identity.redirect_identity_role: NON-IDENTIFYING TRANSPORT PROVENANCE: redirect destinations and the ordered redirect chain MUST NOT replace the discovered identity URL, merge or split items, or re-key source_item_id. Redirect differences alone are NOT identity conflicts; existing independent GUID conflicts remain unchanged.
identity.redirect_topology_change_behavior: for the same provider_id, event_family and normalized official discovery URL, U1 -> U2 then U1 -> U3 yields the SAME canonical_primary_statement_url = normalize(U1) and the SAME source_item_id. Transport movement alone creates neither a logical item nor a content revision: identical body follows same_item_same_body_hash; changed body follows same_item_different_body_hash under that same item.
identity.reobservation_identity_stability: scheduled re-observations retain the stored canonical_primary_statement_url derived from original discovery U1. A request may start from that official identity URL; the final destination observed that day MUST NOT recompute or rewrite item identity. No scheduler, recheck-anchor or deadline semantics change.
identity.revision_id: design rev4: derived from (observation, content_hash, gating timestamps)
identity.rss_guid_role: OFFICIAL DISCOVERY IDENTIFIER AND PROVENANCE ONLY - not business identity, not revision identity, not proof of unchanged content
identity.source_item_id: SHA-256 using canonical_serialization over the ordered JSON array [provider_id, event_family, canonical_primary_statement_url], containing exactly those three string values in that order. No other field participates in the logical item hash or identity dedupe.
identity.source_observation_id: design rev4: derived from (provider, source_item_id, content_hash); NEVER URL alone
identity.uniqueness_claim: NOT contractually documented by the provider; identity quality remains GOOD, not EXCELLENT

invariants.F01: Only official allowlisted Federal Reserve surfaces may contribute.
invariants.F02: RSS is discovery, never source-time authority.
invariants.F03: The primary statement page is the semantic authority.
invariants.F04: declared_release_at requires a strict explicit date PLUS an explicit EST/EDT release grammar; it is NEVER a content visibility gate.
invariants.F06: observed_at is the real primary-statement acquisition instant.
invariants.F08: Raw is made durable before any parse.
invariants.F09: Same logical item with changed bytes appends a new immutable revision. For the same provider_id, event_family and canonical_primary_statement_url, mutable content metadata corrections, including official_statement_date, MUST preserve source_item_id; the prior revision remains intact.
invariants.F10: Same bytes create no duplicate revision.
invariants.F11: Last Update never advances original source availability.
invariants.F12: The provider numeric rate limit remains UNKNOWN; the client ceiling is HyprL policy only.
invariants.F13: Raw redistribution is disabled in V1.
invariants.F14: Unknown upstream correction semantics never imply immutability.
invariants.F16: No market, outcome, consensus or LLM field exists in the capture layer.
invariants.F17: The CaptureSpec hash is bound into every normalized revision.
invariants.F18: Unsupported release syntax never guesses a time: declared_release_at is null with RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED, and the EventRevision is not withheld on that ground.
invariants.F19: RELEASE TIME IS NOT CONTENT-VINTAGE PROOF. A provider-declared logical release timestamp must never be used as the source availability of a captured content revision unless the provider contract proves that exact revision became available at that timestamp. For FOMC V1 no such revision-specific proof exists.
invariants.F20: BACKFILL CONTENT VINTAGE. Historical backfill content is visible only from its actual observed/durable timeline unless exact vintage provenance exists. An original release timestamp may describe event metadata but cannot retroactively date the fetched body.
invariants.F21: REVISION-SPECIFIC AVAILABILITY. A later observed content revision cannot inherit an earlier logical event release timestamp as its own source availability. Each revision requires its own availability evidence; absent provider evidence, source_available_at = null.
invariants.F22: ABSENCE CLAIM CANNOT EXCEED CLASSIFIER COVERAGE. An absence assertion must never cover a semantic family broader than the frozen classifier's proven coverage. Where classifier completeness is not established, zero is scoped to the capture predicate only.
invariants.F23: UNRESOLVED CANDIDATE BLOCKS ZERO. Any discovery item that is a CYCLE_CANDIDATE and cannot be deterministically classified as IN_SCOPE_V1 or DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE blocks EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO for that cycle. No exception. A durably concluded unresolved item is ALREADY_KNOWN for later cycles and stays visible as an unresolved item record.
invariants.F24: DISCOVERY/PRIMARY CLASSIFICATION CONFLICT FAILS CLOSED. If discovery metadata indicates an in-scope candidate but the primary page does not satisfy the frozen predicate: no event, no zero, and no silent downgrade to out-of-scope. Diagnostic and raw provenance are recorded under existing source-health semantics. Scope: the cycle in which the conflict is a CYCLE_CANDIDATE (zero_assertion.cycle_definition).
invariants.F25: MUTABLE CONTENT METADATA MUST NOT DEFINE LOGICAL IDENTITY. Mutable statement metadata parsed from primary-page content, including official_statement_date, MUST NOT participate in source_item_id, the logical item hash or identity dedupe. With provider_id and event_family fixed and the same frozen canonical_primary_statement_url, date corrections preserve the logical item, with or without RSS GUID. Changed bytes append revisions; identical verified bytes under the same CaptureSpec hash must yield the same date, otherwise FAIL CLOSED with no new content revision and no overwrite.
invariants.F26: DISCOVERY URL ANCHORS LOGICAL IDENTITY. For FOMC V1, canonical_primary_statement_url is the official statement link parsed from durable official discovery provenance BEFORE primary redirects, validated and normalized under existing V1 rules. Redirect destinations, final response URLs and HTML canonical URLs are non-identifying provenance and MUST NOT replace this identity input. The rule applies to LIVE feed and HISTORICAL_BACKFILL manifest discovery (surfaces.backfill_manifest), with or without RSS GUID. The admitted HTTPS scheme MUST be serialized as exactly lowercase ASCII https in the identity URL; original scheme spelling MUST NOT be hashed as the scheme component of canonical_primary_statement_url. Apply the existing hostname normalization unchanged and serialize the canonical authority WITHOUT any port component: an absent port and admitted explicit decimal 443 MUST yield the exact same identity URL. Original explicit default-port spelling MUST NOT be hashed as a port component of canonical_primary_statement_url. Any malformed percent escape makes the discovery URL inadmissible: no canonical_primary_statement_url or source_item_id may be derived/admitted from it. Validate percent syntax before normalization/identity and before any request; no repair or percent-decoding is introduced by this gate.
invariants.F27: TRANSPORT REDIRECTION MUST NOT REKEY AN ITEM. With provider_id, event_family and the normalized official discovery URL fixed, U1 -> U2 and later U1 -> U3 MUST produce the same source_item_id from normalize(U1). Transport movement alone cannot split logical history, cause an identity conflict or create a content revision; changed bytes append revisions under the same item, and unchanged bytes do not duplicate revisions.
invariants.F28: HTTPS SCHEME CASE CANNOT ALTER LOGICAL IDENTITY. HTTPS scheme admission is ASCII case-insensitive; the canonical identity scheme is always exactly lowercase ASCII https. With provider_id, event_family and every other URL component unchanged, changing only upstream HTTPS scheme case MUST preserve canonical_primary_statement_url and source_item_id and MUST NOT create an identity conflict or content revision. Non-HTTPS and empty/missing schemes are rejected, never silently upgraded. Original source spelling is raw discovery provenance only.
invariants.F29: EXPLICIT DEFAULT HTTPS PORT CANNOT ALTER LOGICAL IDENTITY. For otherwise identical admitted official discovery URLs, with provider_id and event_family fixed, an absent port and explicit decimal port 443 MUST produce byte-identical canonical_primary_statement_url values WITHOUT a port component and the SAME source_item_id. Default-port spelling alone MUST NOT create a logical item, identity conflict or content revision. Any other explicit port or malformed port is rejected before source_item_id derivation and before any request; never silently stripped, rewritten or interpreted as absent/default. Raw explicit-port spelling remains provenance only.
invariants.F30: MALFORMED PERCENT ESCAPES ARE REJECTED BEFORE IDENTITY OR REQUEST. Every literal % in an admitted V1 URL must begin PCT_ENCODED = % HEXDIG HEXDIG, with exactly two ASCII hex digits from 0-9, A-F or a-f. Otherwise FAIL CLOSED before canonical identity/source_item_id derivation or admission, before a primary request, and before redirect follow. This mandatory syntax gate does not decode, re-encode, repair or provide a literal-percent fallback. Valid escapes remain subject to existing component restrictions and path-preservation semantics; no new equivalence or hex-case normalization is introduced. Durable raw source text is not mutated.
invariants.F31: DECODED BODY SIZE IS ENFORCED DURING PRODUCTION. For every body consumed under V1's existing decoded-size policy, count decoded entity-body bytes incrementally from zero before charset/text decoding. Enforce the feed 2097152-byte or statement 5242880-byte cap during bounded output production, not after unbounded decompression. If the next output would exceed the cap, stop body decoding immediately, do not append excess bytes and do not continue to learn final size. Exactly the cap passes the size gate; cap + 1 rejects. Content-Length or compressed size cannot replace this gate. No oversized body or incomplete prefix reaches text decoding, XML/HTML parsing or normalization, becomes a complete admitted raw artifact or successful complete-body hash, or produces an EventRevision. Reuse PARSER_FAILED, never EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO. Existing successful-body hash/persistence/replay bytes and raw-first order remain unchanged.
invariants.F32: TEXT DECODING IS SINGLE-VALUED AND STRICT UTF-8. Both V1 XML and HTML bodies use only UTF-8, also the explicit default when signals are absent. Every recognized HTTP/BOM/document encoding signal must be UTF-8-compatible under text_decoding_v1, or cause PARSER_FAILED; labels are limited to utf-8 and utf8 after the frozen ASCII-only label normalization. No competing authority, heuristic detection, fallback decoder, lossy error handling or platform codec/alias selection. Invalid UTF-8 and unsupported BOMs fail closed. Exactly one leading UTF-8 BOM is an encoding signature omitted from semantic text, never removed from raw/hash/replay bytes. Same verified admitted bytes plus persisted relevant HTTP metadata plus the same CaptureSpec hash MUST produce the same Unicode text or PARSER_FAILED. Charset failure preserves raw provenance, creates no EventRevision and cannot establish zero for an affected feed/candidate. Existing Unicode/whitespace transformations and FIX1-FIX8 remain unchanged.
invariants.F33: HTML SEMANTIC ANCHORS ARE UNIQUE AND AUTHORITATIVE. primary_page_title is the unique h3.title within the frozen article-heading region; official_statement_date the unique p.article__time; release_line the unique p.releaseTime start element. No document-metadata, inline-SVG, global-text or traversal-order fallback may substitute. Zero or more than one title or date match: PARSER_FAILED; zero or more than one release-line match: non-gating RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED.
invariants.F34: RELEASE LINE EXTENT IS TOKEN-BOUND, NOT RECOVERED-DOM-BOUND. release_line consists only of the leading character-data segment following the unique p.releaseTime start tag and preceding the next markup token. Recovered descendant .textContent is forbidden as authority. This closes the observed unclosed-paragraph problem.
invariants.F35: SEMANTIC TEXT NORMALIZATION ORDER IS SINGLE-VALUED: (1) character-reference-aware field extraction, (2) NFC, (3) ASCII-whitespace collapse, (4) U+0020 trim, (5) exact compare or strict parse. No reordering.
invariants.F36: XML DISCOVERY PARSING HAS NO DTD / CUSTOM-ENTITY / XINCLUDE EXPANSION PATH. FOMC V1 discovery XML forbids DOCTYPE and XInclude. External DTDs, external general entities and external parameter entities are never resolved. Custom internal entity declarations are unsupported because DOCTYPE is forbidden, so the billion-laughs family is rejected before expansion. Parsing performs no network or filesystem resolution. Security rejection is PARSER_FAILED and blocks EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO.
invariants.F37: HTTP BODY SIZE BOUNDS AND XML EXPANSION SECURITY ARE DISTINCT. The FIX8 feed cap of 2097152 bytes applies to decoded HTTP input bytes. XML parser safety does NOT rely on that cap to bound entity or XInclude expansion; parser-level amplification mechanisms are forbidden outright by FIX11.
invariants.F38: ONLY FINAL HTTP 200 CAN PRODUCE AN ADMITTED CONTENT BODY. Only exact final status 200 may enter the normal body, hash, text-decoding, parser and revision pipeline. Any other final status is non-admitted and cannot produce an EventRevision or a clean zero. Body appearance never overrides status.
invariants.F39: PARTIAL / EMPTY / NOT-MODIFIED RESPONSES CANNOT MASQUERADE AS COMPLETE CONTENT. 206, 204 and 304 are unsupported and non-admitted in V1. No prior-body reuse on 304, no Range requests, no conditional requests, and no successful complete-body hash or revision from any of these statuses.
invariants.F40: REDIRECT FOLLOWING IS EXPLICITLY BOUNDED AND NON-IDENTIFYING. Only 301, 302, 303, 307 and 308 may be followed, at most 3 transitions, with every target security-validated before the request. The fourth redirect target is never requested. Redirect bodies are non-semantic and identity remains the pre-redirect official discovery URL.
invariants.F41: CACHE VALIDATORS ARE PROVENANCE, NEVER CONTENT-VINTAGE PROOF. ETag, Last-Modified and HTTP caching metadata cannot populate or infer causal content-availability timestamps. Conditional requests are disabled in V1.
invariants.F42: REDIRECT LOCATION IS RESOLVED AGAINST THE CURRENT REQUEST URL BEFORE SECURITY VALIDATION. Location is an HTTP URI-reference; relative and scheme-relative references are supported. The base is the actual absolute request URL of the CURRENT redirect hop and advances with each hop. Resolution occurs before target security validation, and the resolved absolute target must then satisfy all existing V1 URL admission rules. No browser repair, no identity effect.
invariants.F43: REDIRECT REFERENCE RESOLUTION CANNOT WEAKEN URL SECURITY. Relative resolution may never bypass HTTPS-only, the host allowlist, the userinfo prohibition, port rules, the query prohibition, percent-escape validation or the fragment non-request semantics. An unsafe resolved target is never contacted.
invariants.F44: PROVIDER RATE ACCOUNTING COUNTS PHYSICAL ATTEMPT STARTS, NOT LOGICAL FETCHES. Each independently attempted HTTP request under the FOMC V1 provider consumes exactly one PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START unit when permission to begin is granted, BEFORE network side effects, with no refund on failure. Feed, primary, every followed redirect, permitted later reattempt, scheduled recheck and historical provider GET all count. A logical fetch with three redirect follows consumes four units; rejected or unfollowed targets create no additional attempt or unit.
invariants.F45: ALL FOMC V1 NETWORK CATEGORIES SHARE ONE PROVIDER ACCOUNTING DOMAIN. Every physical attempt passes through the same FEDERAL_RESERVE_PROVIDER_V1_GLOBAL accounting/limiter gate. Independent feed, primary, recheck, redirect and historical quota buckets are forbidden; redirect/retry internals and category-specific queues cannot bypass aggregate provider admission. No logical fetch reserves a multi-request corridor.
invariants.F46: PROVIDER RATE CEILING USES A ROLLING 60-SECOND PHYSICAL-START WINDOW. For candidate monotonic t, include prior admitted s iff 0 < t - s < 60; admission requires at most five such prior starts. For every admitted t, (t-60s,t] contains at most six PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START events. At t=60 after starts 0,10,20,30,40,50, start 0 is excluded and candidate 60 is admitted if spacing and epoch preconditions pass. No fixed-minute, token-bucket or leaky-bucket substitute.
invariants.F47: MINIMUM SPACING IS PROVIDER-WIDE START-TO-START. A candidate requires t - previous_start >= 10 seconds; exact equality passes. Accounting, window and spacing use the SAME PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START atomic grant-and-consume event immediately before transport invocation. Completion time cannot shift the reference. No category or redirect/recheck exemption, no stored or reusable permit and no refund after grant, including cancellation before network I/O.
invariants.F48: RATE ADMISSION IS ATOMIC AND MONOTONIC WITHIN A LIMITER EPOCH. All concurrent candidates, across every FOMC V1 category/process emitter, pass through one provider-wide atomic inspect/test/grant/register decision over comparable monotonic history before transport. Stale-state double grants and simultaneous starts are forbidden; later candidates see prior grants. UTC/NTP/manual/timezone/DST changes cannot alter elapsed admission. The coordination primitive is unspecified.
invariants.F49: NEW LIMITER EPOCHS FAIL CONSERVATIVELY CLOSED FOR 60 SECONDS. Every fresh limiter epoch requires exclusive provider ownership and no attempt for its first 60 monotonic seconds; exact elapsed 60 passes the embargo. The epoch embargo begins only once old independent issuers can no longer initiate attempts. Independent overlapping epochs cannot both emit. After embargo, admission uses fresh current-epoch history; precise prior-epoch monotonic history is not reused and durable per-request history is not required. UTC history cannot shorten the embargo.
invariants.F50: REOBSERVATION GRID IS ANCHORED TO THE FIRST DURABLE PRIMARY OBSERVATION'S observed_at. For each logical FOMC source item, the original anchor is exactly observed_at of the first (smallest commit_seq) qualifying LIVE, clock-check-passing admitted complete primary content observation that reaches existing durable raw/SourceObservation persistence. Request/header time, raw durability commit, normalized/EventRevision commit, declared_release_at, ingested_at, limiter monotonic start and restart time cannot replace that value. Semantic parse success and EventRevision commit are not prerequisites. The anchor is immutable across later observations/revisions; targets remain original observed_at plus exactly 300,3600,86400,604800 seconds with existing precision. No source_available_at inference.
invariants.F51: DURABILITY DETERMINES ANCHOR SURVIVAL, NOT ANCHOR TIME. A volatile observation lost before the required raw/SourceObservation durability boundary creates no reconstructible anchor. Once the qualifying observation is durable, its original observed_at remains the anchor across crashes and restarts, even before normalized commit and after downstream parser/normalization failure. No restart-relative or commit-relative re-anchoring, no inferred anchor from lost volatile state, and no later revision or limiter delay may shift the grid.
invariants.F52: DURABLE REOBSERVATION ANCHOR IMPLIES FOUR REQUIRED LOGICAL OBLIGATIONS. At the existing qualifying original anchor durability boundary, exactly four logical obligations exist for offsets 300,3600,86400,604800 and targets original observed_at plus offset. No scheduler-specific write or normalized EventRevision commit is required for logical existence. Missing or partial materialization and crash after anchor durability cannot erase them; without a qualifying durable anchor no set can be derived from a lost volatile observation. This freezes membership, not execution or completion.
invariants.F53: REOBSERVATION OBLIGATION IDENTITY IS DERIVED AND IDEMPOTENT. The authoritative logical key is (source_item_id, original_reobservation_anchor_observed_at, offset_seconds), using exclusively the original FIX16 anchor and one of the four fixed offsets. Repeated/concurrent recovery, materialization, lost materialization ACK, same-body reobservation, parser recovery and H1 -> H2 cannot add logical checkpoints or a second grid. Duplicate rows denote the same member; different source items with equal anchor times remain distinct. Physical encoding and status/completion semantics are not prescribed.
invariants.F54: PAST-DUE OBLIGATIONS REMAIN REQUIRED. A PENDING reobservation obligation stays required after due_at, with no MISSED, EXPIRED, FAILED or other terminal state from lateness or failure (a SUSPENDED retry episode is a work-item state, not an obligation status). After downtime it becomes eligible subject to selection and FIX15, and is satisfied only by a real later observation with its own observed_at; no backdating, synthesis or due_at rewrite, and late execution never shifts any target.
invariants.F55: ONE DURABLE REOBSERVATION MAY SATISFY ALL DUE OBLIGATIONS FOR ITS ITEM. A qualifying observation R of S satisfies exactly the obligations of S with due_at <= R.observed_at, never those with a later due_at and never another item's. Several overdue obligations produce one logical fetch, not catch-up GETs, and satisfaction claims no earlier source state.
invariants.F56: OBLIGATION SATISFACTION OCCURS AT THE DURABLE SOURCE OBSERVATION BOUNDARY. Satisfaction requires a per-response record of an admitted final exact-200 complete primary response with canonical observed_at that reached durable raw/SourceObservation persistence. Changed content, parse success, a new EventRevision and normalized commit are not required; a durable observation followed by parser failure satisfies the obligation while health records PARSER_FAILED.
invariants.F57: FAILED ATTEMPTS DO NOT SATISFY OR ERASE OBLIGATIONS. Transport, deadline, redirect, non-200, incomplete, content-coding, oversize, persistence-loss, clock-anomaly and cancellation outcomes leave the obligation PENDING. Further provider work follows BOUNDED_RETRY_EPISODE_V1: at most 6 logical fetches per episode (backoff 60/300/900/3600/14400 s), then SUSPENDED; no tight loop, no hidden retry.
invariants.F58: SATISFACTION IS CRASH- AND ACK-RECONSTRUCTIBLE. Obligation status is derived only from the durable anchor and durable qualifying observation records. Completion rows are caches; losing a marker or an ACK never causes a provider request, and a volatile observation lost before durability satisfies nothing.
invariants.F59: FEED, REOBSERVATION AND BACKFILL WORK CANNOT STARVE EACH OTHER. All work shares the FIX15 limiter. Class rotation derives from durable dispatch records; within classes (next_eligible_at, source_item_id) ordering and suspending bounded episodes guarantee service. Queue pressure, restart or later feed contents never delete required work.
invariants.F60: EVERY PHYSICAL NETWORK ATTEMPT HAS A 60-SECOND ACTIVITY-INDEPENDENT TOTAL DEADLINE. It starts at PHYSICAL_REQUEST_ATTEMPT_START after limiter waiting, is monotonic, never resets on received bytes, and covers DNS, TCP, TLS, request write, headers, body and content decoding. Connect 10 s and read-inactivity 30 s still apply and the earliest limit wins. Each redirect-follow attempt has its own deadline. Expiry aborts logically: a late DNS result is discarded, no TCP connection or HTTP byte follows, nothing is admitted, and it maps to SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.
invariants.F61: ZERO IS CYCLE-LOCAL AND FAILURES BLOCK IT. EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO holds for one LIVE discovery cycle iff its feed observation qualifies and every item is DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE or ALREADY_KNOWN in the durable pre-cycle state (commit_seq < B). Any CYCLE_CANDIDATE - unresolved, conflicting, unidentifiable, or with an unconcluded LIVE acquisition - makes the cycle NOT_ZERO. The conclusion is durable and never rewritten; backfill never blocks it.
invariants.F62: EST/EDT ARE LITERAL FIXED-OFFSET SOURCE LABELS AND RELEASE-CLOCK PARSING IS NON-GATING. EST = UTC-05:00 and EDT = UTC-04:00 regardless of season, with no timezone database. Any other, missing or malformed release clock gives declared_release_at = null and RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED; no zone is guessed and the EventRevision is not withheld.
invariants.F63: STATEMENT RELEVANCE IS STRUCTURAL THEN SEMANTIC. Feed items outside the statement-family path prefix with non-matching titles are DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE; in-family items are candidates; only exact feed title plus PRIMARY_STATEMENT_PATH_V1 (monetary<valid YYYYMMDD>a.htm) triggers a primary GET; the page title decides admission.
invariants.F64: NEWER UNNORMALIZED CONTENT IS NEVER HIDDEN. Revisions are keyed per content hash. The current normalized revision is the one matching the latest durable qualifying observation's hash (reused after A-B-A); when none exists, NEWER_DURABLE_SOURCE_CONTENT_UNNORMALIZED holds and no older revision may be presented as current source truth. No revision is invented and no content is discarded.
invariants.F65: PROVIDER RETRY TRAFFIC IS FINITE AND DURABLE. Every work item retries in bounded episodes whose state derives from durable dispatch/outcome records; restart never resets an episode; episode opening is keyed by offsets, not wall time; an anchored dead item costs at most 120 autonomous physical requests.
invariants.F66: LOCAL FAILURE NEVER CAUSES EXTRA PROVIDER TRAFFIC. Commit and corruption failures cause none; lost-bytes persistence failure counts as one attempt of the bounded episode, exactly like a crash; without a committable dispatch record no request can start.
invariants.F67: REDIRECTS ARE FOLLOWED ONLY BY A MANUAL LOOP. Automatic client redirect following is non-conforming; each hop is validated before contact, takes its own limiter grant and deadline, and at most 3 are followed. No existing repo opener is claimed to conform.
invariants.F68: HISTORICAL BACKFILL IS A FINITE MANIFEST WITHOUT A RECHECK GRID. Backfill input is a validated, deduplicated, ordered manifest of at most 1000 primary statement URLs; no listing page is crawled; backfill observations never create anchors or obligations and never suppress LIVE acquisition; observation_mode is per observation.
invariants.F69: DURABLE ACQUISITION WORK SURVIVES FEED DISAPPEARANCE. A LIVE acquisition created by a cycle stays required until concluded or suspended, whatever later feeds list.
invariants.F70: TIMESTAMPS ARE CANONICAL AND COMPARED AS INSTANTS. All FOMC timestamps use CANONICAL_UTC_TIMESTAMP_V1 (market_data_store._canonical_timestamp); arithmetic and ordering use parsed instants, and 'first/earliest/latest' between durable records means commit_seq order.
invariants.F71: COLLECTOR CLOCK ANOMALIES FAIL SAFE. An observation failing COLLECTOR_CLOCK_CHECK_V1 (90 s against server Date + Age when present; otherwise 60 s against the latest trusted reference and 90 s against the epoch record) keeps its observed_at but is never processed, cannot anchor, satisfy or start a cycle, is a visible diagnostic, and never becomes a reference.
invariants.F72: RAW CORRUPTION FAILS CLOSED EVERYWHERE. A digest mismatch found in processing, recovery, reconciliation or replay prevents parsing, yields CORRUPTION_FAIL_CLOSED, marks dependent revisions NORMALIZED_PRESENT_RAW_CORRUPT and never triggers a refetch.

item_predicate.backfill_discovery_side: a HISTORICAL_BACKFILL_MANIFEST_V1 entry satisfies the discovery-side conjunct for its backfill observations only; primary_page_title_exact still decides

classification_states.DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE: the item is excluded by a frozen deterministic negative rule that requires NO semantic guessing. V1 keeps this category deliberately NARROW.
classification_states.IN_SCOPE_V1: the exact frozen positive predicate succeeds on BOTH surfaces
classification_states.UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE: the item appears on the official monetary-policy discovery surface, does not satisfy the positive V1 predicate, and cannot be proven outside the broader monetary/FOMC domain without semantic guessing

item_predicate.default_rationale: fail closed. Unknown relevance resolves to UNRESOLVED, never to a negative. There is no frozen safe negative rule for a differently-titled official monetary item, so the default applies.
item_predicate.evidence: title verified on the four FOMC statement feed items and on statement pages sampled 2015-2026

feed_item_classification_v1.already_known: an identifiable item is ALREADY_KNOWN iff, in the pre-cycle state, EITHER (a) KNOWN_ADMITTED: it has a committed IN_SCOPE_V1 EventRevision in any observation mode; OR (b) KNOWN_CONCLUDED: it has a durable feed item conclusion UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE or classification conflict, or a terminal non-normalized processing outcome from a qualifying LIVE observation, AND it has no unconcluded LIVE acquisition, AND NOT (it has no qualifying LIVE observation while its current feed title == feed_title_exact and its path matches PRIMARY_STATEMENT_PATH_V1). The last clause makes an item retitled to the exact statement title a CYCLE_CANDIDATE again (step 6).
feed_item_classification_v1.applies_to: every item of a LIVE discovery cycle's feed observation, evaluated against the pre-cycle state (zero_assertion.cycle_definition.pre_cycle_state)
feed_item_classification_v1.durable_conclusions: each UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE conclusion made by these steps is persisted as a feed item conclusion record within the cycle conclusion transaction
feed_item_classification_v1.live_after_backfill: an item KNOWN_ADMITTED only through HISTORICAL_BACKFILL, with no qualifying LIVE observation, receives exactly one LIVE acquisition under step 3 when the feed lists it with the exact title and path; that acquisition never makes any cycle non-zero and never counts as newly admitted
feed_item_classification_v1.negative_rule_scope: the only frozen negative rule is structural (step 2). No title-based negative rule exists; in-family items with other titles stay UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE and block the cycle in which they are first concluded.
feed_item_classification_v1.persistence_of_conclusions: items concluded UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE by steps 4, 5 or 6 are KNOWN_CONCLUDED in later cycles (step 3); only step-1 items (no identity) block every cycle that lists them
feed_item_classification_v1.retitle: an item previously concluded UNRESOLVED from feed fields whose feed title becomes exactly the statement title, with a PRIMARY_STATEMENT_PATH_V1 path and no qualifying LIVE observation, is a CYCLE_CANDIDATE and gets a LIVE acquisition; the cycle is NOT_ZERO
steps: 1. link fails V1 URL admission or identity derivation -> CYCLE_CANDIDATE, concluded UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE (unidentifiable); it has no source_item_id, so it is a CYCLE_CANDIDATE in every cycle that lists it
2. canonical path outside the prefix of surfaces.statement_family_path AND normalized feed title != feed_title_exact -> DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE (structural negative rule; non-blocking)

3. the item is ALREADY_KNOWN in the pre-cycle state -> KNOWN (non-blocking, never newly admitted). If it is KNOWN_ADMITTED only through HISTORICAL_BACKFILL, has no qualifying LIVE observation and no LIVE acquisition record, and its feed title == feed_title_exact and path matches PRIMARY_STATEMENT_PATH_V1, one LIVE acquisition is created (live_after_backfill); this does not make it a CYCLE_CANDIDATE
4. canonical path outside the prefix AND feed title == feed_title_exact -> CYCLE_CANDIDATE, concluded UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE
5. path under the prefix but not matching STATEMENT_FAMILY_PATH_V1 -> CYCLE_CANDIDATE, concluded UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE (malformed family)

6. otherwise CYCLE_CANDIDATE: if feed title == feed_title_exact AND path matches PRIMARY_STATEMENT_PATH_V1 -> it needs a LIVE acquisition (created unless an unconcluded one exists); else concluded UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE from feed fields
feed_item_classification_v1.unconcluded_acquisition_blocks: an item that is not KNOWN_ADMITTED and has a LIVE acquisition that is not concluded (pending, in flight, failing or SUSPENDED) is a CYCLE_CANDIDATE in every cycle that lists it; a KNOWN_ADMITTED item never blocks, whatever the state of its LIVE acquisition

item_predicate.known_v1_narrowness: an unscheduled or differently-titled FOMC action is NOT captured by V1. It is recorded as an UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE, makes its cycle non-zero and stays durably visible as an unresolved item record; it is never silently treated as absent. Widening the positive predicate requires a spec revision.
item_predicate.no_broad_semantic_classifier: V1 must NOT be widened with keyword lists, semantic similarity, an LLM, regex over body text, or hardcoded emergency-action vocabulary. Honest incompleteness beats speculative coverage.
item_predicate.normalization: extract from parser_policy.primary_page_title_anchor, then apply parser_policy.semantic_text_normalization in its frozen order; comparison is exact and case-sensitive
item_predicate.on_positive_predicate_no_match: classification = UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE unless the structural negative rule (feed_item_classification_v1 step 2) proves DEFINITELY_OUT_OF_SCOPE. No normalized FOMC EventRevision is created either way. An UNRESOLVED_CANDIDATE blocks EVENTS_OBSERVED_ZERO for the cycle in which it is a CYCLE_CANDIDATE; once durably concluded it is ALREADY_KNOWN for later cycles.
item_predicate.role: POSITIVE CLASSIFIER FOR THE V1 SUBSET ONLY - a non-match is NOT proof that an item is not an FOMC monetary-policy event
item_predicate.rule: CONJUNCTION - both must hold, on verified official fields only
item_predicate.superseded_rule: rev2 said a non-match was "NOT an FOMC event" - a definitive negative that allowed a false zero. Withdrawn in rev3.

HISTORICAL_BACKFILL.logical_release_metadata: SUPPORTED when the strict parser succeeds

LIVE.logical_release_metadata: SUPPORTED when the strict parser succeeds

mode_capabilities.no_blanket_flag: there is deliberately no ambiguous "retrospective supported" boolean anywhere in this spec

HISTORICAL_BACKFILL.discovery: surfaces.backfill_manifest (HISTORICAL_BACKFILL_MANIFEST_V1) only; URLs never synthesised from dates; no archive/calendar crawl
HISTORICAL_BACKFILL.raw_first: the manifest artefact is persisted durably before any backfill request
HISTORICAL_BACKFILL.relabelling: a backfill item is NEVER relabelled LIVE

modes.live_not_preempted: a backfill observation never suppresses LIVE acquisition: an item KNOWN only through HISTORICAL_BACKFILL, without a qualifying LIVE observation, is LIVE-acquired when the feed lists it with the exact statement title and a PRIMARY_STATEMENT_PATH_V1 path (feed_item_classification_v1 step 3); with another title it is not fetched in LIVE
modes.mode_is_per_observation: observation_mode belongs to each per-response record and each EventRevision (from its source observation). Logical source identity is mode-neutral; an item is never labelled BACKFILL or LIVE as a whole.
modes.reconstruction: observed_at is NEVER reconstructed from source timestamps in either mode

normalized_field_notes.canonical_source_url: the existing normalized field carries canonical_primary_statement_url = the normalized official discovery link BEFORE primary redirects; it is not final_response_url or HTML canonical. No schema rename or expansion.
normalized_field_notes.capture_scope_id: binds the deterministic V1 capture subset so downstream cannot confuse provider family with coverage completeness
normalized_field_notes.classification_state: IN_SCOPE_V1 for any admitted revision; the other states never produce a revision
normalized_field_notes.declared_release_at: provider release metadata; NEVER a revision visibility gate
normalized_field_notes.official_statement_date: required normalized metadata of the observed content revision, NEVER logical identity. Date authority and validation remain timestamps.source_date; a date parse failure follows the existing parser/source-health policy. Removing the identity role does not make the date optional.
normalized_field_notes.source_item_id: stable logical identity from provider_id, event_family and the current canonical_primary_statement_url only; official_statement_date is separate revision metadata

anchor_cardinality_failure.distinction: STRUCTURAL extraction failure of the TITLE or DATE anchor - absent or duplicated - is PARSER_FAILED. Release-line anchor failures (absent, duplicated, empty or multiple declarations) are NON-GATING RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED under timestamps.unrecognised_release_syntax. A successful unique title extraction that merely differs from the expected title keeps the FIX2 classification/conflict semantics.
anchor_cardinality_failure.zero_policy: a title or date anchor failure of a CYCLE_CANDIDATE's primary page leaves its acquisition concluded non-normalized; the cycle containing that candidate is NOT_ZERO. A broken template can never mean "no FOMC statement".

anchor_drift_policy.historical_templates: NO claim is made that these anchors hold for 2015, 2019, all Federal Reserve history or all monetary pages. Pages whose TITLE or DATE anchors do not match FAIL CLOSED; a non-matching release-line anchor is non-gating RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED. FIX10 adds no legacy selector.
anchor_drift_policy.immediate_release_note: no 'For immediate release' page was captured in the evidence sample, so its DOM placement is not empirically exercised. If it appears in the SAME frozen p.releaseTime anchor the existing grammar applies; otherwise the release line is non-gating RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED (timestamps.unrecognised_release_syntax), never a guess.
anchor_drift_policy.on_cardinality_violation: TITLE or DATE anchor: FAIL CLOSED / PARSER_FAILED. RELEASE-LINE anchor: non-gating RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED (timestamps.unrecognised_release_syntax).
anchor_drift_policy.rationale: intentional provider drift detection: if upstream markup changes, V1 must stop rather than guess

parser_policy.determinism: operates offline on verified locally stored raw body bytes and the persisted relevant HTTP Content-Type provenance required by text_decoding_v1; the same bytes, metadata and CaptureSpec hash must yield the same decoded text or PARSER_FAILED. No network or machine-dependent charset selection.

html_semantic_anchors.superseded: rev10 listed three bare names ("official statement date", "page title / event family", "release line") with no DOM authority, which R10 found could make two conforming implementations classify every statement oppositely

html_semantic_region.layout_classes_not_required: the observed heading container also carried col-xs-12 col-sm-8 col-md-8. Those are presentational and are NOT required; only the heading class token is.
html_semantic_region.relation_justification: the evidence records the full observed path div#article / div.heading.col-xs-12.col-sm-8.col-md-8 / {h3.title | p.article__time | p.releaseTime} on 5/5 pages, so the DIRECT_CHILD relation is what the evidence proves and is not a strengthening beyond it.

parser_policy.identity_url_input: supplied by identity.identity_url_authority from durable official discovery provenance; never parsed from primary HTML as a semantic anchor. HTML canonical handling is identity.html_canonical_role.
parser_policy.llm: FORBIDDEN anywhere in ingestion - an LLM may not decide whether something is an FOMC statement, nor its date, release time, identity, revision or source authority

official_statement_date_anchor.duplicate_rule: even two identical duplicate dates are structural ambiguity -> PARSER_FAILED; no value-based dedupe
official_statement_date_anchor.identity_role: UNCHANGED - remains revision metadata and NON-IDENTIFYING per FIX3

Its DISPLAYED VALUE equalled the statement date on all 5 samples, so only STRUCTURE can distinguish them - a value check never could.

official_statement_date_determinism.failure: PARSER/NORMALIZER DETERMINISM FAILURE is a diagnostic, not a new global source-health state. FAIL CLOSED for parser/spec inconsistency or corruption: no second content revision, no silent normalized mutation; existing raw and immutable revisions remain intact.
official_statement_date_determinism.rule: identical verified persisted primary raw body bytes under the SAME CaptureSpec hash MUST yield identical official_statement_date metadata. A differing date with the same verified body hash is not an upstream content revision.

primary_page_title_anchor.comparison: exact string comparison against "Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement" after the frozen normalization pipeline. No contains, startswith, endswith, case-insensitive, fuzzy match or prefix-stripping heuristic.
primary_page_title_anchor.document_title_negative_control: the HTML document <title> is NOT the classifier authority on two independent evidenced grounds: its observed text is "Federal Reserve Board - Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement", which is PREFIXED and fails the exact predicate; and the selector is NOT UNIQUE - every sampled page carried a second <title>Lock</title> inside an inline SVG banner icon. A generic <title> lookup is therefore forbidden.
primary_page_title_anchor.document_title_permitted_use: diagnostics/provenance only; it can neither satisfy nor break the classifier

release_line_anchor.character_references: resolved to Unicode as part of extraction, BEFORE NFC; extraction never extends through later markup because descendant text exists
release_line_anchor.duplicate_rule: two p.releaseTime start tags -> RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED (non-gating, timestamps.unrecognised_release_syntax) even if their text is identical; no first/last wins
release_line_anchor.empty_leading_segment: if the unique start tag exists but no non-whitespace semantic character data precedes the first subsequent markup token: RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED (non-gating, timestamps.unrecognised_release_syntax). No fallback to descendant text and no later scan of the page.
release_line_anchor.multiple_declarations_in_segment: the single extracted segment must satisfy exactly one strict release declaration grammar; ambiguous or multiple independent declarations -> RELEASE_TIME_UNPARSED (non-gating, timestamps.unrecognised_release_syntax), never first-match selection.
release_line_anchor.observed_result: only the release declaration plus its surrounding raw whitespace; the <ul> and everything after it is excluded
release_line_anchor.text_extent_rule: after locating the UNIQUE p.releaseTime START TAG in the decoded HTML token stream, release_line_source_text is the concatenation of the contiguous character-data / character-reference-derived text immediately following that start tag and preceding the FIRST subsequent HTML markup token. That first markup token terminates the segment.
release_line_anchor.tokenization_requirement: no parser library is pinned, but deterministic HTML tokenization sufficient to distinguish START TAG, CHARACTER DATA, CHARACTER REFERENCE and the next MARKUP TOKEN is required. Comments, declarations and tags after the start tag all terminate the segment. A parser that has already repaired the DOM in a way that loses this original token boundary may NOT substitute repaired .textContent. A tokenizer/event stream or an equivalent structural scan over the decoded HTML is acceptable provided these semantics are exact.
release_line_anchor.why_token_bound:
the evidence shows p.releaseTime is NEVER CLOSED: there is no
